questions.question: Which animal is this?
questions.explanation: Axolotls can regrow lost legs, and in the wild they live only in the lakes and canals around Mexico City.

questions.question: Which animal is this?
questions.explanation: Despite its name, the red panda is not a close relative of the giant panda, and it spends most of its life up in the trees.

media.alt: A furry animal with a stripy tail

questions.question: Which animal is this?
questions.explanation: The capybara is the biggest rodent in the world, and it loves to wallow in water.

media.alt: A large brown animal with a blunt nose
media.credit: Photo: Giles Laurent, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which bird is this?
questions.explanation: Puffins dig burrows to nest in on cliff tops, including around the coasts of Britain.

media.alt: A black and white seabird with a colourful beak
media.credit: Photo: Charles J. Sharp, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which animal is this?
questions.explanation: The platypus is one of the very few mammals that lay eggs.

media.alt: A furry animal swimming in water
media.credit: Photo: Charles J. Sharp, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: What is a baby kangaroo called?
questions.explanation: A newborn joey is about the size of a jellybean, and it crawls straight into its mother's pouch.

questions.question: What does a giant panda spend most of its day eating?
questions.explanation: A giant panda can spend more than ten hours a day munching bamboo.

questions.question: How many hearts does an octopus have?
questions.explanation: Two of its hearts pump blood through its gills, and the third pumps it round the rest of its body.

questions.question: What colour is a polar bear's skin under its fur?
questions.explanation: Under its thick coat a polar bear has black skin, and its hairs are actually see-through rather than white.

questions.question: Which bird can fly backwards?
questions.explanation: Hummingbirds beat their wings so fast that they can hover in one spot, and even fly backwards.

questions.question: What is a group of lions called?
questions.explanation: The lionesses in a pride do most of the hunting, often working together as a team.

questions.question: What does a snake use its flicking tongue for?
questions.explanation: Its tongue picks up smells from the air and carries them to a special sensing spot in the roof of its mouth.

questions.question: What is the biggest animal alive today?
questions.explanation: A fully grown blue whale can be longer than a tennis court.

questions.question: Which farm animal has a stomach split into four parts?
questions.explanation: The four parts of a cow's stomach help it break down tough grass, and it brings food back up to chew again as cud.

questions.question: Which bird lays the biggest eggs?
questions.explanation: One ostrich egg weighs about as much as two dozen hen's eggs.

questions.question: Which animal is this?
questions.explanation: Despite its zebra-striped legs, the okapi's closest living relative is the giraffe.

media.alt: A brown forest animal with striped legs
media.credit: Photo: Daniel Jolivet, CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which animal is this?
questions.explanation: The aye-aye taps on trees with its long, thin middle finger to find grubs, and it lives only on Madagascar.

media.alt: A wide-eyed animal with large ears clinging to a branch

questions.question: Which bird is this?
questions.explanation: The shoebill is a huge, slow-moving bird of African swamps, named for its bill shaped like a big clog.

media.alt: A tall grey bird with an enormous bill
media.credit: Photo: Bob Owen, CC BY 2.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which animal is this?
questions.explanation: The saiga's big, drooping nose filters out dust in summer and warms up icy air in winter on the steppes of Central Asia.

media.alt: A pale antelope with an unusual drooping nose
media.credit: Photo: Andrey Giljov, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: Which animal is this?
questions.explanation: The Komodo dragon is the largest lizard alive today, found on just a handful of Indonesian islands.

media.alt: A large lizard walking on the ground
media.credit: Photo: James Jolokia (james1203), CC BY 4.0 (Wikimedia Commons)

questions.question: What is the collective noun for a group of crows?
questions.explanation: A parliament is a group of owls, an unkindness is ravens, and a charm is goldfinches.

questions.question: Which bird has the longest wingspan of any living bird?
questions.explanation: A wandering albatross can have wings more than three metres from tip to tip, and it glides for hours without flapping.

questions.question: What is a male bee called?
questions.explanation: Drones have no sting and do not gather nectar or pollen; their main job is to mate with a queen.

questions.question: In which part of the world do narwhals live?
questions.explanation: A narwhal's famous tusk is really a long spiral tooth that can grow longer than two metres.

questions.question: The tuatara, a reptile with a light-sensing 'third eye' on top of its head, lives in the wild only in which country?
questions.explanation: The tuatara is the last survivor of a group of reptiles that lived alongside the dinosaurs.

questions.question: Which is the fastest bird in a hunting dive?
questions.explanation: Diving after prey, a peregrine falcon can top 300 km/h, faster than any other animal.

questions.question: Which animal's young are called elvers?
questions.explanation: Young European eels drift thousands of miles from the Sargasso Sea before swimming up rivers as elvers.

questions.question: Which mammal has the longest pregnancy?
questions.explanation: An elephant calf takes about 22 months to arrive, nearly two years.

questions.question: Which tiny animal is better known by the nickname 'water bear'?
questions.explanation: Tardigrades, usually about half a millimetre long, can survive being dried out, frozen and even exposed to open space.

questions.question: What is a female fox called?
questions.explanation: Red foxes have learned to live in towns and cities all over Britain.
